cards.text: This psalm is a song for the choirmaster, and the singer is calling out to the WHOLE planet. "Make a joyful noise to God, all the earth!" Not a polite little hum, friend. A NOISE.

cards.question: The singer wants the whole earth singing. What should all that singing celebrate?

cards.text: Then the singer hands everybody the exact words to say to God: "How awesome are Your deeds!" It's like a coworker passing you the birthday card AND telling you what to write in it.

cards.question: The singer says God's power is so great that His enemies ___ before Him.
In the words the singer gives the earth to say to God, only a few nations bow down to Him.

cards.text: Then comes a Selah, and a brand new invitation: "Come and see the works of God; how awesome are His deeds toward mankind." Not come and HEAR about it, friend. Come and SEE. Bring your eyes.

cards.question: To show God's awesome deeds, the singer points back to a time at the sea. What did God do to the sea?
They passed through the waters on foot, and the singer says they rejoiced in God right there.

cards.text: Did you catch that little word "we" in there? The singer tells it like a family that's told Grandpa's big story so many times, EVERYBODY at the table starts saying "we."

cards.question: God rules forever by His power, and His eyes watch the nations. So the rebellious should not ___ themselves.

cards.text: Another Selah. Then the call goes out even wider: "Bless our God, O peoples; let the sound of His praise be heard."

cards.question: The singer gives a reason to bless God: He preserves their lives. And He keeps their feet from doing what?

cards.text: Then the song takes a turn. The singer talks straight to God, and suddenly it's not all sunshine and joyful noise anymore.

cards.question: The singer tells God that He tested them and refined them like silver.

cards.text: The singer keeps going: "You led us into the net; You laid burdens on our backs." Friend, I know a little something about being stuck where you didn't plan to be. ASK the junk drawer.

cards.question: Men rode over their heads, and they went through fire and water. But where did God bring them in the end?

cards.text: Now the song switches from "we" to "I." The singer is headed into God's house with burnt offerings, ready to fulfill some vows.

cards.question: The singer has vows to fulfill at God's house. When were those vows first spoken?

cards.text: We've ALL made a promise like that on the side of a highway: "Lord, get me home and I'll never skip an oil change again." The difference is, this singer actually shows up to keep it, while that oil change light is STILL ON.

cards.question: To keep those vows, the singer plans to bring God a small and simple offering.

cards.text: Fatlings, rams, bulls AND goats, with the fragrant smoke going up. That's not a thank-you card, friend, that's the whole barnyard RSVPing yes. Selah.
Then the singer turns to the crowd with a new invitation. And this time? It's personal.

cards.question: The singer is about to declare what God has done for them. Who gets invited to come and listen?
The singer's story starts with crying out to God, and praise came right along with that cry.
The singer gets serious about prayer: if ___ had been cherished in the heart, the Lord would not have listened.
The singer says God heard the prayer but didn't pay attention to it.

cards.text: God HEARD that prayer and paid attention to the sound of it, friend. Not left on read, not "seen at 3:42," HEARD.

cards.question: The singer sums it all up in one last line. How does the song end?

answers.text: Blessing God for His loving devotion
Asking God for one more sign

cards.text: It started with the whole earth making a joyful noise, and it ends with one singer and one answered prayer. Same God, big enough for all the earth and still listening to one voice.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: the setup, the quote, "Not a polite little hum, friend." and "A NOISE."

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: the quote line, "Not come and HEAR about it, friend.", "Come and SEE." and "Bring your eyes."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The statement says "they rejoiced," but the text says "there we rejoiced in Him" (Ps 66:6). The text switches from "they" to "we," and the card blurs that switch. Card 9 then builds a joke on that switch.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card asks "Did you catch that little word 'we' in there?" No earlier card ever showed the baker the word "we." Card 8 even says "they rejoiced." So the callback has no setup.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: This card tells nothing new. It comments again on Ps 66:6, which cards 7 and 8 already covered, so it doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The Grandpa's-story comparison says the singer is retelling an event he wasn't at, like family members repeating an old story. The text never says how the "they" who passed through the waters connects to the "we" who rejoiced.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "So the rebellious should not ___ themselves" adds a cause-and-effect link with "So." The text only sets the two lines side by side: "His eyes watch the nations. Do not let the rebellious exalt themselves" (Ps 66:7).

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "hide" can be argued right. The question just said God's eyes watch the nations, so a baker could reason that the rebellious shouldn't try to hide from Him.

rule.text: If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: "Then the call goes out even wider" isn't true. Verse 1 already called "all the earth," so "O peoples" (Ps 66:8) isn't wider.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: "The singer gives a reason to bless God: He preserves their lives" calls Ps 66:9 the reason for Ps 66:8. The text doesn't say it is. It simply follows.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quote line, "Friend, I know a little something..." and "ASK the junk drawer."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This card is only a joke. It tells nothing from Ps 66:13-14 that cards 1 and 2 hadn't already covered, yet it cites those verses.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: "This singer actually shows up to keep it" states as done what the text gives only as a future intention: "I will enter Your house... I will fulfill my vows" (Ps 66:13).

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the list of offerings, the barnyard joke and "Selah."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Then the singer turns to the crowd with a new invitation.", "And this time?" and "It's personal."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This card restates Ps 66:19, which card 10 just tested (God heard and paid attention). It's a recap with a joke and doesn't move the passage forward.

The last card sums up the whole psalm (cited Ps 66:1-20) instead of telling part of the passage. Also, "one answered prayer" stretches the text. Verses 19-20 say God heard, attended to and did not reject the prayer. They never say what was asked or that it was granted.
